title: Inferred Context Prioritizer — compact repr notes
summary: Personal sketch for a compact representation and API shape for ranking/inferencing which pieces of client context to keep hot (KV cache/prefetch) vs evict, balancing cost and signal importance.
content:
Goal:
Define a small, transportable representation for a 'context candidate' that can be cheaply evaluated by routing and admission-control tiers to prioritize prewarm, caching, and batching. Needs to be: compact, mostly numeric/categorical, stable across minor prompt edits, and explainable for debugging and SLO/qos tracing.

Motivation/background:
- Current prefix-KV heuristics are simple (LRU, recency, token-count-weighting) and miss semantic importance (e.g., user identity blobs vs transient system prompts).
- We want a unified prioritizer that feeds: ingress router (for warm lane decisions), prefetch scheduler, and on-node admission control.

Representation (proto-ish, compact):
- id: stable-hash(str)  // 64-bit hex string (deriveable on client and server)
- score_features: [f1..fN]  // dense float vector (N <= 16) quantized to int8 for transport
- tags: ["user-profile","persona","system-seed","tool-output"]  // small set of enums
- length_tokens: integer
- last_seen_ts: iso8601 string
- origin: enum {client, proxy, server-prefetch}  // small enum
- provenance: short-hint-string  // e.g. "chat-turn-7/assistant-reply"

Notes on features: score_features is the meat — designed to be cheap features, not full embeddings. Example feature list proposal (order matters):
  0: semantic-salience (0..1 float)  // heuristic from token salience + named-entity weighting
  1: user-stability (0..1)  // how often this blob recurs for this user
  2: recency-decay (0..1)
  3: downstream-cost-sensitivity (0..1)  // if token cost is high, prefer compact reprs
  4: session-affinity-score (0..1)
  5: instruction-likelihood (0..1)  // fraction of tokens that look like instructions
  6..15: reserved/learned features (quantized)

Transport considerations:
- Pack as CBOR or msgpack; store score_features as bytes (int8). Keep whole repr <= 256 bytes to allow propagation in headers (when needed) and store in lightweight routing caches.
- Fallback: if client cannot compute score_features, server will compute server-side and return id for later reuse.

API shapes (HTTP/JSON examples):
1) POST /v1/context-candidates/evaluate
   body: {"candidates": [{"id":"abc123","length_tokens":58,"tags":["persona"],"origin":"client","provenance":"turn-3"}], "target_model":"gpt-small"}
   resp: {"evaluated": [{"id":"abc123","priority":0.87,"reason_tags":["high-stability","persona"],"ttl_seconds":3600}], "meta":{"computed_by":"router-2a"}}

2) GET /v1/context-candidates/{id}  -> returns last-known repr + last priority

Decision logic sketch (router-side):
- Combined score = w1*semantic-salience + w2*user-stability + w3*session-affinity - w4*cost_penalty(length_tokens, downstream-cost-sensitivity)
- We keep weight defaults in a small policy object; can be overridden per-tenant via Dedicated/Private configs.

Prefetch integration:
- Prefetch scheduler accepts prioritized list and budget tokens/time. It will ask evaluator for marginal benefit estimate. Marginal benefit function can be a learned small model (on serving-runtime side) that consumes the compact vector.

Admission control and tracing:
- When eviction happens, we log the compact repr id + reason to tracing payload (span attribute) so RCA can reconstruct why particular context was dropped.
- Provide debug endpoint that given a request id returns candidate reprs considered and their weighted contributions.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to keep id stable across client-side formatting changes (e.g., whitespace)? Use canonicalization + hashing strategy.
- What privacy considerations for shipping user-stability feature? If this is sensitive, only server-side compute allowed.
- Need experiments: simulate heatmaps on production traces to see distribution of compact repr sizes and feature variance.

Mini ASCII architecture diagram:
client -> ingress-router [evaluate reprs] -> prefetch-scheduler -> warm-pool / forward to serving-node
                                
router keeps short cache (id -> last priority) and forwards repr bytes to scheduler when budget allows

Experiment plan (next steps):
- Small offline eval on anonymized session logs: compute score_features (server) for 100k candidates, measure corr with downstream reuse (is this candidate reused within 30m?).
- Build lightweight evaluator in router (no NN: linear weights) as feature gating baseline.
- Add ability to toggle client-side compute in SDK; default off for first rollout.

Implementation notes (quick):
- Keep proto forward-compatible: reserve bytes for future features; always allow missing features interpreted as 0.
- Use existing tokenization pipeline for length_tokens and instruction-likelihood heuristics.

Notes to self: keep representation minimal — the primary win is being able to ship a tiny vector that is cheap to evaluate in the fast-path router. Avoid full embeddings unless we implement a separate embedding-based lane.

References/related docs (internal):
- runtime-telemetry-annotator-sketch (for tracing attributes)
- prefetCH-sla-broker-api-sketch (for scheduler integration)

End of scratchpad.
